correctness.rationale: Exact tests of all 65536 vertex subsets with two equivalent predicates, followed by complete finite acyclic Morse matchings on 59818 (Shrikhande) and 59746 (rook) nonempty faces, produce critical dimensions (0:1,9:11) and (0:1,9:1,11:2). A separate reverse-order matching gives the same counts. Forman gives the 11-fold ninth sphere wedge for Shrikhande; the rook Morse CW model gives torsion-free homology in degrees nine and eleven without assuming null higher attachments. All 192 graph automorphisms are exhaustively identified by affine symmetries and local rigidity; signed simplicial and independent orbit Lefschetz computations agree elementwise. Their sum is zero and squared sum is 576, proving the asserted invariant and character inner product. All witness scripts and records are included in the package.

originality.rationale: The archived forest-complex reductions and general Alexander duality do not classify this non-chordal strongly regular example. Full inspected same-graph results cover independent-set or closed-neighborhood containment simplices, not the dominance noncontainment simplices, and do not supply the full automorphism character. Indexed queries under direct names, closed-neighborhood hypergraph alias and complement-neighborhood dual return no dominating theorem. This is positive novelty evidence relative to inspected literature, not a claim that nonappearance in search proves priority.
residual_risks: No indexed-search result can rule out an unindexed or unpublished equivalent exact complex calculation.
The dual neighborhood-complex formulation creates a plausible route for an independently published but differently named computation.
The source comparisons establish best-knowledge originality only, not independently verified priority.

value.rationale: A canonical exceptional strongly regular graph and its cospectral rook twin share full basic graph parameters and dominance face vectors through degree ten, but exhibit different integral homology groups. The new Shrikhande exact homotopy type and its complete 192-element rational symmetry character, including zero invariants and multiplicity-free decomposition, refine previously published independence and Čech comparisons in a mathematically natural new complex. The numerical target is motivated by a well-known two-class graph exception, rather than an arbitrary graph slice.
